item.title: Is the mudslide along the China-Nepal border linked to climate change?
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
Is the mudslide along the China-Nepal border linked to climate change? Following a mudslide at Gyirong Port, located along the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, experts have weighed in on whether climate change was a contributing factor. According to a specialist, the disaster is closely tied to global warming. Rising temperatures have accelerated the melting of glaciers. The combined effects of glacial retreat, local geological and geomorphological conditions, and broader climatic factors are believed to have been the primary triggers. The disaster was further complicated by a chain reaction involving ice and rock collapses. These cascading events, together with the inherent difficulties of managing cross-border disaster prevention, make risk reduction in high-altitude regions particularly challenging. Climate change is continuously reshaping the cryosphere and its ecosystems, environment, and disaster patterns worldwide. On the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, glaciers are shrinking and retreating at an accelerating rate, creating an important backdrop for the increasing frequency of geological disasters in the region. Drawing on more than six decades of data from three comprehensive glacier inventories conducted in China, researchers have gained a clear picture of this shrinking trend. These findings provide a solid data foundation for monitoring and early warning systems. The first inventory recorded a total glacier area of 51,000 square kilometers on the plateau. By the second inventory, that figure had declined to 44,000 square kilometers. According to the most recently completed third inventory, the plateau's glacier area has now dropped to 39,000 square kilometers. Kang Shichang, director and researcher at the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan province, said that glaciers across the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau have shrunk by 24 percent in area over the past 60 years, a decline of nearly a quarter. "The retreat has been particularly pronounced in the southern part of the plateau. In areas including the Gangdise Mountains, Nyenchen Tanglha Mountains, and Himalayas, glaciers have shrunk by about 40 percent over the past 60 years. The main driver of this dramatic change is global warming," Kang said. The ongoing melting of glaciers has directly led to a substantial increase in both the number and size of glacial lakes across the plateau. This has greatly heightened the risk of glacial lake outburst floods, landslides, and other disasters. There are now more than 14,000 glacial lakes on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, covering a combined area of over 1,100 square kilometers. Overall, these lakes continue to expand rapidly, with associated disaster risks steadily accumulating. Nie Yong, another researcher at the same institute, said glacial lakes across the plateau have expanded markedly in recent decades, with the most pronounced growth occurring in the Himalayan region along China's southern border. The area of glacial lakes in the region is expanding by an average of about 1% annually. These continuously expanding lakes have become the primary source of geological disaster risks in high-altitude areas. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: SCO poised to play a greater role in building a community with a shared future for humanity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
SCO poised to play a greater role in building a community with a shared future for humanity Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept. 1 attended the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and the "SCO Plus" meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, where he delivered important remarks. His speech set a clear direction for the SCO to pursue higher-quality development and for the international community to jointly advance an equal and orderly multipolar world, as well as a more just and equitable system of global governance. Twenty-five years ago, reckoning with the hard lessons of the Cold War, confronting the real threats from terrorist, separatist and extremist forces, and heeding the earnest aspirations of the world for peace and development, the SCO was established and gradually showed its vitality. Over the past 25 years, the SCO has grown from six founding members into a large family spanning 27 countries across Asia, Europe, and Africa. It has gradually become a new type of regional cooperation organization -- one with the largest land area and population of such bodies, and with enormous development potential. The SCO has pioneered and has consistently upheld the Shanghai Spirit of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations, and pursuit of common development. It has found the right way of coexistence, featuring non-alliance, non-confrontation, and not targeting any third party. It brings countries in the region together to build a common home and successfully set a stellar example in conducting relations among big countries, among neighbors, and among countries of different sizes. In today's world, transformations unseen in a century are accelerating. The competition between dialogue and confrontation, win-win and zero-sum mindsets, and multilateralism and unilateralism is intensifying. At this crossroads, where the future of humanity hangs in the balance, the SCO must step forward, shoulder its historical responsibility, and steer the course ahead. During the summit in Bishkek, Xi, focusing on the future of humanity, raised four proposals. He said the SCO should stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity; it should stay committed to taking security as a key goal, and foster an environment of common security; it should stay committed to a people-centered approach, and cement the foundation for everlasting friendship; it should stay committed to dialogue and consultation, and strive for more equitable and orderly governance. Grounded in the profound changes of the times and aligned with the trend of history, these four proposals provide fundamental guidance for the SCO to build consensus, deepen cooperation, and pursue steady and sustained progress under the new circumstances. In recent years, the rise of the Global South is bringing about profound changes in the international balance of power. The trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible. At the "SCO Plus" meeting, Xi stressed that as a responsible major country, China advocates for an equal and orderly multipolar world. Sovereign equality and mutual respect are fundamental principles. Balance, order and the rule of law are inherent requirements. Multilateralism, dialogue and consultation are essential pathways. Mutual benefit, win-win, and inclusiveness are the way forward for development. To make the SCO more united and dynamic, and to enable it to play a greater role in advancing an equal and orderly multipolar world, Xi proposed to advance common prosperity in the vast continent straddling Asia and Europe with the SCO Strength, to promote the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom, and to guide the reform and improvement of global governance through the SCO Action. These proposals inject strong positive energy into SCO member states and partners as they grasp the underlying trend of history, shoulder the responsibilities of the times and work together to build a more just and equitable system of global governance. As a founding member, China has always been an important force in advancing the development and growth of the SCO. China will implement 100 technological cooperation projects with other SCO countries in the next three years, and support the early opening of the SCO's four security centers so as to upgrade the capacity of member states in responding to security threats and challenges. It will establish a China-SCO basic education cooperation center, and continue to build bridges for exchanges, mutual learning and people-to-people connectivity through Confucius Institutes, Luban Workshops and other programs, support the SCO in conducting exemplary cooperation on implementing the Global Governance Initiative, and call for continued improvement of the SCO's institutional mechanism to enhance its efficiency in decision-making and implementation. All sides highly appreciated China's important contribution to the development of the organization and agreed to actively implement the strategic blueprint laid out at the 2025 SCO Summit in China's Tianjin. They agreed to continue carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit, improve institutional mechanisms, strengthen political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in trade, investment, science and technology, energy, finance, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity, bring peoples closer together, and work together to address new security challenges, so as to write a new chapter of lasting peace and common development. Standing at a new starting point on the 25th anniversary of the SCO, China will work with all parties to continue to hold high the banner of the Shanghai Spirit, implement the development strategy of the SCO for the next decade, and pursue development with higher quality, so as to make greater contributions to a community with a shared future for humanity. item.title: China and Nepal join forces in cross-border disaster response
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
China and Nepal join forces in cross-border disaster response A Chinese tunnel-rescue expert (right) works with Nepalese personnel on a search-and-rescue operation in Nepal's disaster-hit area. (Photo courtesy of the Chinese tunnel‑rescue expert team) On the morning of Aug. 26, the Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, was hit by a severe mudslide that occurred on the Nepalese side of the border. In the aftermath, Chinese authorities in meteorology, water resources, and natural resources swiftly coordinated with their Nepalese counterparts. They shared real-time monitoring data and provided meteorological and hydrological products and services to support joint efforts to respond to the disaster. Located on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, Gyirong Port is characterized by high elevation, complex terrain, and highly variable weather conditions. "From late August to early September this year, cold air has been particularly active across the plateau, especially along the border areas. This has led to frequent precipitation and posed severe challenges to rescue efforts," explained Ma Xuekuan, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Center. "At noon on Aug. 26, after receiving a request from Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, we organized the first joint consultation that same afternoon. On the afternoon of Aug. 31, we held a second joint consultation with the Nepalese side," said Zhang Tianhang, a senior engineer at the World Meteorological Center Beijing. The two sides had previously set up a WeChat working group to share relevant information in real time. The emergency consultation on Aug. 26 was conducted via the MAZU (multi-hazard, alert, zero-gap, and universal) cloud-based meteorological early warning system. Experts from both sides jointly assessed weather conditions and analyzed the trajectory of subsequent precipitation. The China Meteorological Administration (CMA) subsequently set up a dedicated task force to provide ongoing meteorological support for Nepal, issuing a daily English-language briefing on meteorological monitoring and forecasting information. For real-time monitoring, the briefings include infrared cloud imagery from China's Fengyun meteorological satellites, as well as products showing real-time temperature and precipitation around the disaster-affected area at a spatial resolution of 1 kilometer. At the request of the Nepalese side, the latest briefing also included lightning monitoring products based on Fengyun satellite data. For forecasting, the CMA mainly provides seven-day weather forecasts for areas near the disaster site, also at a one-kilometer resolution, along with areal precipitation forecasts for the next three and seven days. "In addition, we have continued to update extended-range forecasts covering 15 to 30 days. Overall, we have provided the Nepalese side with seamless forecasting services covering the next 30 days, offering strong support for its rescue efforts," Zhang said. Following the disaster, a barrier lake formed near the confluence where the Cuojian River from Nepal meets the Purepuqiang Zangbo River on Chinese territory. China's Ministry of Water Resources immediately dispatched an emergency hydrological monitoring team to the front line. Working alongside staff from the bureau of hydrology and water resources survey of Xizang, the team carried out hydrological monitoring, forecasting and early‑warning operations. A Chinese tunnel-rescue expert (left) works with Nepalese personnel on a search-and-rescue operation in Nepal's disaster-hit area. (Photo courtesy of the Chinese tunnel‑rescue expert team) At present, the Ministry of Water Resources provides the Nepalese side with daily updates in five areas: the development of the barrier lake on the Purepuqiang Zangbo River; risk assessments of potential chain reactions caused by the impact craters along the Cuojian River; risk screening for glacial lakes in the Gyirong Zangbo River basin; forecasts of the development and risks of newly formed barrier lakes; and information from hydrological emergency monitoring. The information provides strong support for emergency response and rescue efforts downstream on the Nepalese side. Across Nepal, only 17 meteorological observation stations are shared with international organizations, resulting in insufficient observation coverage. China has built the world's largest integrated, three-dimensional meteorological observation system incorporating space-, air- and ground-based capabilities. Its advanced observation equipment, including Fengyun meteorological satellites and weather radars, provides strong monitoring capabilities. Following the disaster, the CMA immediately made arrangements to strengthen monitoring. On the evening of Aug. 26, it deployed small ground-based observation stations around the disaster-affected area. On Sept. 1, it deployed a mobile weather radar near the affected area. To address gaps in Nepal's meteorological monitoring capabilities, the CMA also accelerated development of a customized version of the MAZU platform for Nepal, completing it before the second joint consultation and continuously improving it in response to Nepalese needs. A large volume of meteorological monitoring products and observation data has since been shared with Nepal through the customized version of MAZU. China's MAZU AI-powered meteorological early warning solution played an important role in the response to the disaster, providing timely support for Nepal's rescue efforts and earning a positive response from the Nepalese side. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology of Nepal sent a letter to the CMA expressing its appreciation. Going forward, building on the sound cooperation between the two sides, China is willing to provide Nepal with meteorological equipment such as radars and ground observation stations to further strengthen the latter's meteorological observation capabilities and work with it to develop a one-stop early warning solution. Following the disaster, the CMA also immediately activated its international user service response mechanism for Fengyun meteorological satellites, providing the disaster-affected area in Nepal with rapid-scan Fengyun satellite products featuring a spatial resolution of 250 meters and a temporal resolution of one minute, as well as multiple high-resolution forecasting products. The China Aero Geophysical Survey and Remote Sensing Center for Natural Resources also coordinated the use of nearly 100 public-service and commercial satellites to scan the disaster-affected area and surrounding regions at high frequency. Experts rapidly assessed the location, causes and evolution, scope of impact and scale of the disaster, and promptly released relevant information to the public. A mudslide may destroy homes, but it cannot break the bonds of solidarity and mutual assistance. The sharing of monitoring information and products has provided strong support for rescue efforts by both China and Nepal, demonstrating the two countries' determination to work together in responding to natural disasters and their shared hope of rebuilding homes. item.title: China's top grain-producing province turns paddies into tourist destinations
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
China's top grain-producing province turns paddies into tourist destinations This photo taken on July 29, 2026 shows a panoramic view of rice paddy art pieces at a rice park in Fujin City, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. (Xinhua) HARBIN, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Surrounded by four rice paddy art pieces stretching across the vast fields in northeast China, a giant piece in the form of a QR code catches many people's attention. It can be scanned to access an online store for agricultural products. These art pieces, spanning 120,000 square meters, are located in a rice park in the city of Fujin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. Heilongjiang, China's top grain-producing province, has transformed vast paddies into thriving tourism destinations, boosting local incomes. Turning a design into a giant field canvas requires multiple steps, including design, positioning, layout marking and transplanting. Rice varieties are selected to match the palette: black rice for black and brown sections, edible rice for green, and ornamental rice for yellow and white. However, this form of art was far less precise in its early days. "When we first tried in 2017, field positioning relied entirely on manual labor. Workers even had to stand high with megaphones to direct the placement," said Wang Chao, head of the office at the Fujin Tourism Development Service Center. "The designs were mostly flat. Now, GPS positioning and 3D composition techniques have made the lines and layers much sharper," Wang noted. This rice landscape is drawing growing numbers of visitors. Zhao Zihan, a tourist from the neighboring city of Shuangyashan, visited the spot in Fujin with her family on a Saturday. "I've passed by several times but never had the chance to stop. This time I came specifically to see it," she said. "The vast rice paddy art lifts my spirit and fills me with hope for the future." Beyond admiring the scene, visitors can now engage in increasingly diverse and immersive experiences, from transplanting rice and milling grain to exploring rice growth and camping beside the paddies. Many of the park's service staff come from surrounding villages, and the visitor flow has spurred the growth of nearby farmstay restaurants. Wang said related services earn participating villagers across 10 villages an extra 4,000 yuan (about 590 U.S. dollars) per person each year. The story of agritourism is unfolding across Heilongjiang's vast landscape. In Xinghuo Village, a Korean ethnic village in Huachuan County, the transformation is vivid. Home to 407 households and over 7,400 mu (around 493 hectares) of farmland, the village sits beside a highway amid scenic surroundings, yet was once just an ordinary village focused on rice cultivation. "Back then, the roads were mostly dirt paths. There was no work for me in the village, so I had to go out and make my way," said Han Liuhua, 45, who left for cities like Shanghai and Qingdao, both in east China, at age 18. In 2018, she gave up her urban career and returned to the village, becoming the first migrant worker to come back in over 20 years. "When I first opened the restaurant in 2022, the villagers weren't very optimistic about me. Visitor numbers were low back then," Han said, noting that the scenic area has since brought a surge in foot traffic, and the restaurant's daily sales can now reach more than 16,000 yuan. "The distance from my office to my restaurant is less than 50 meters. But when tourists are at their peak, it takes me five minutes just to squeeze through," Han said. "I'm one of the biggest beneficiaries of the village's transformation." In 2025, the village's scenic area opened, welcoming 1.33 million visitors, generating 300 million yuan in revenue across the full industrial chain, and creating jobs for over 800 people. The scenic area has renovated farmhouse exteriors in the traditional Korean style, built ecological picking gardens, and created an 8,000-square-meter giant rice paddy art piece to develop diversified, immersive and year-round products. Inside the park, visitors can immerse themselves in Korean ethnic culture and agricultural experiences, from making kimchi and brewing rice wine to transplanting and harvesting rice. The same trend is unfolding elsewhere in the province. In the city of Wuchang, a renowned rice-growing area, local enterprises are also actively developing agritourism products. "I often come here after work. Rice has always been close to my heart, and seeing the vast paddies is far more relaxing than visiting a regular park," said a local resident surnamed Hu, who was picnicking at Qiaofu Dayuan Agricultural Co., Ltd. The company hosts a variety of rice culture events each year, including rice-planting festivals and harvest ceremonies, while also serving as an experimental education base for primary school students, welcoming tens of thousands of visitors from across the country annually. "Premium rice isn't just about taste. It is about the experience," said Qiao Wenzhi, head of the company, adding that by combining product customization with experiential value, the premium for their rice has risen by up to 40 percent. Heilongjiang's broader push for agritourism also comes as China moves to diversify its tourism offerings and cultivate new growth drivers for the industry. "Developing the multiple functions of agriculture" has been incorporated as a measure in the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), referring to efforts to ensure food security and supply while integrating agriculture with culture and tourism. The latest five-year tourism development plan, approved by the State Council and released in July 2026, calls for nurturing new drivers of tourism growth and enriching the supply of high-quality tourism experiences. item.title: Over 2,500 rescuers deployed to mudslide-hit border port in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
Over 2,500 rescuers deployed to mudslide-hit border port in China's Xizang A drone photo taken on Sept. 6, 2026 shows rescuers working at the core affected zone of the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Tenzin Nyida) GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- China has deployed more than 2,500 rescue personnel after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, the emergency response and rescue headquarters said on Sunday. The mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, had left 43 people dead and 519 others missing at the border port as of 6 p.m. Saturday, officials told a press conference. As of 6 p.m. Saturday, more than 2,500 people and over 500 vehicles had been deployed to join rescue operations, and more than 1,000 flights of drones had air-dropped 5.43 tonnes of supplies, officials said. item.title: Book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization published
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
Book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization published BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization has been published by the Higher Education Press and the People's Publishing House. Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has approached ecological conservation from the perspective of ensuring the sustainable development of the Chinese nation. With a profound understanding of the important position and strategic significance of ecological conservation in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era, the CPC Central Committee has vigorously advanced theoretical, practical and institutional innovation in this field, put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking and new strategies, led historic, transformative and comprehensive changes in China's ecological conservation, and developed Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization. The book introducing the thought, compiled under the organization of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee and the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, consists of an introduction and nine chapters, totaling about 170,000 Chinese characters. It systematically expounds on the significance, theoretical framework, essence, connotations and practical requirements of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization.
